A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JET research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated analyses and case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original truncation experiments, trained-model benchmark results, rollout and reward analyses, training measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds reward ablations, KL-divergence measurements, error-correction analysis, and Llama/Pangu evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed two-stage rollout, progressive truncation, correctness-conditioned weighted linear reward, and DAPO objective remain unchanged. Additional backbones, alternative-reward descriptions, and NPU implementation adaptations do not establish a changed JET learning procedure.

E1.justification: The documented MATH/DAPO-MATH training mixture and eight evaluation benchmarks are retained. The added Llama and Pangu experiments reuse existing mathematical tasks; correctness-stratified MATH500 analysis also introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The matched benchmark comparisons retain the same baseline methods, and the new backbone evaluations use existing comparator types. However, v3 Section 4.7 announces a Sigmoid reward comparison while Figure 5 and Table 4 still report only Ours, Linear, and Exp. Whether Sigmoid was actually evaluated cannot be verified.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-8B and Pangu-Embedded-7B evaluation configurations. The Pangu experiment uses all 1,319 GSM8K test problems, greedy decoding, and an 8,000-token cap. It also introduces the error-correction metric, correctness-stratified pilot reporting, and new reward controls. These extend the evaluation design; the existing Qwen protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analysis of correcting initially wrong answers, JET-versus-DAPO KL dynamics, reward-coefficient sensitivity, and rewarding incorrect versus only correct answers (Sections 2.2, 4.5, C.4–C.5). These examine previously untested aspects of the justification and reward design. Conversely, Figure 3 drops the GSM8K and aggregate rollout-ablation panels. Existing curriculum, difficulty, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten independent repetitions for AIME 2024 and AMC. v3 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practice; its additional results remain point estimates or training curves.

E6.justification: The main Qwen tables and existing reward-strategy accuracy table retain identical values. v3 adds Llama results, reward-ablation results, KL curves, and Pangu results; Table 7 reports 94.69% accuracy and 1,462 tokens against its base model's 94.77% and 1,662. Figure 1 replaces pooled length statistics with correctness-stratified results and reports error-correction rates of 10%, 12.5%, and 22.5%. Some rollout-ablation results are removed from Figure 3.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 introduces a formal probability-factorization and importance-ratio argument for truncated rollouts, assuming a short forced suffix and non-negligible suffix probability under the old policy. Equations 10–12 argue for distribution preservation and stable updates. v1 has no corresponding theoretical argument; this is substantial new mathematical content, although its final approximation is insufficiently justified.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central efficiency, accuracy, and proactive-stopping claims. The introduction adds a distinct theoretical contribution claiming that truncation preserves effective learning signals and permits reliable learning from shortened trajectories.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations attributing unfavorable reward settings to reward hacking, gradient-scale imbalance, and conflicting signals from incorrect answers. It interprets lower KL as distribution preservation and extends applicability claims to additional model families and Ascend hardware. These substantially expand the mechanistic and applicability discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds Ascend hardware and software versions, tensor-parallel settings, compiler restrictions, and model-forward adaptations. The original GPU and core training details remain. However, v3 removes v1's checkpoint-release statement and two direct Hugging Face checkpoint links; the GitHub code link remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds Arora and Zanette's efficient-reasoning work for the Sigmoid reward and Chen et al.'s Pangu-Embedded paper. It removes a short related-work discussion of GRPO, DAPO, and Dr.GRPO, while retaining the underlying cited works elsewhere. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the contributions, rollout explanation, and results discussion, plus reorganized appendix subsections and new theory, platform-validation, and LLM-usage sections. Much of the introduction, objective description, conclusion, and existing appendix prose remains unchanged, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands into three panels, and Figure 3 replaces two rollout panels with a KL plot. v3 adds a Pareto visualization and four tables covering Llama results, reward ablations, NPU configuration, and Pangu results. The main benchmark tables exchange order, and existing appendix displays move around the additions. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The reward ablations and additional model/platform evaluations provide useful empirical support missing from v1. However, the newly promoted theoretical contribution in Section 3.3 does not establish its central conclusion: a short suffix and near-one token ratios do not ensure a near-one sequence ratio. The undocumented Sigmoid comparison and removal of checkpoint links also weaken reporting. These empirical benefits and rigor/reproducibility setbacks leave the net quality direction uncertain.
